cause.detail: restoreCommonGroundForWorld on a world with NO CommonGround payload calls settleCommonGroundIfNothingStaged, adding the world to restoreSettledWorlds; an empty live snapshot may then lawfully save. Later, in the SAME session, a PRESENT payload is read and staged for that world. stageCommonGroundWorldPayload set pendingByWorld but did NOT invalidate the older settled membership. If commonGroundSnapshot then rejects the payload (foreign actor, wrong world, malformed), it consumes the pending bytes and leaves an empty local snapshot. isPristineCommonGround now sees no pending, sees the stale settled bit and answers false, so saveWorld serializes idle over the raw payload just read off disk. The pre-existing cold foreign-payload test never had an earlier empty restore in-session, so it could not see this.

fix.change: A non-null (PRESENT) staged payload now also deletes the world from restoreSettledWorlds. A newer present read cannot borrow ownership from an older ABSENT answer; ownership must be re-earned either by real validation (markCommonGroundRestoreSettled on hydration) or by a later read that genuinely finds nothing (settleCommonGroundIfNothingStaged). raw == null keeps the existing behaviour exactly: pending is cleared and nothing is invalidated.
